innovations.name: Roadmap into the STEM working environment
innovations.lead: Initiative Junge Forscherinnen und Forscher e.V.
innovations.problem:
The world of work and the labour market are undergoing profound change due to increasing technologization and digitalization - traditional training paths are disappearing or changing, while new or modified job profiles with new skills requirements are constantly emerging. This also presents the Bavarian education system with the major challenge of preparing all young people to successfully navigate an increasingly complex and unpredictable (professional) future and to find their way through the wide range of training and career opportunities. Modern STEM education, which combines specialist skills with overarching future skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving and learning skills or the ability to collaborate, is a crucial cornerstone for future and labor market viability. STEM professions continue to offer very good labor market prospects and career opportunities for individuals. In terms of society as a whole, however, a sufficient pool of STEM specialists is the key driver of innovation and crisis resilience in Bavaria - especially in the face of critical challenges such as decarbonization & climate protection or the further development of digitalization1.
Due to the actuality of the subject described above, the number of different STEM offerings for children and young people has been increasing significantly for some time. As a result, the so-called “STEM learning ecosystem” (= the sum of learning and experience opportunities through school, extracurricular activities, career guidance services, the Internet, museums, internships, family support, etc.)2 in which every student moves is becoming increasingly diverse. Nevertheless, numerous studies show a clear need for action and needs among children and young people in the areas of STEM skills development and career orientation:
- The new STEM-influenced world of work and the associated attractive and future-oriented professions and developments have not yet been sufficiently understood by pupils; their career ideas therefore often do not meet the requirements of the labor market3 - Many students do not feel sufficiently informed about the prospects and career opportunities of STEM subjects4 or are overwhelmed by the variety of career information available5 - Socially and educationally disadvantaged pupils in particular often completely lack realistic, sustainable career prospects, which has a negative impact on their academic performance6 or focus on careers that are subject to a high risk of automation or are below their talents3 - Girls often develop inadequate and clichéd ideas about STEM careers as early as primary school age and therefore often do not include them in their later career choices7; they also feel less competent in STEM than they actually are8 - Science skills among primary school pupils are below the OECD average9, young people show declining STEM skills and a third are considered underperforming in terms of digital skills8
What is particularly striking is the problematic lack of orientation with regard to their own professional future, which is increasingly prevalent among the educationally disadvantaged. Recent long-term studies provide clear recommendations on what adolescents need in order to develop prospects, have an easier transition into the (STEM) job market and have better chances of employment, better salaries and greater satisfaction in later working life6,10. All children and young people must have the opportunity as early and often as possible along the entire education chain
- to test and expand their own STEM and future skills through educational methods that are tailored to the target group and generate interest (such as inquiry-based learning, project-based learning) - experience the changing world of work with its new, attractive working methods and job profiles in a stereotype-free and authentic way in order to broaden their professional horizons and develop future-proof, realistic prospects adapted to the labor market; this
innovations.description:
In a new, innovative project in Bavaria, the IJF would like to develop, establish, test and disseminate such a system for the broad-based promotion of STEM skills and interests among pupils along the education chain. The IJF acts as an agile, external education provider in cooperation with the Ministry of Education and Cultural Affairs in regular lessons and thus reaches not only pupils interested in STEM, but also a large number of those for whom one or more of the aforementioned needs have not yet been (sufficiently) met. innovations.name: Design Wings
innovations.problem: The apprentice designers who completed their studies in 2018-2022 were invited to participate in the project because, as the employees of the creative segment, they were affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and lost their income and the possibility to improve their professional skills. During the project, they receive scholarships, improve their professional skills, and develop professional ethics while collaborating with the enterprise. The other group benefiting from the project are representatives of small and medium-size businesses who do not have the possibility to employ designers paying them the market price. Professional design solutions created during the project help to increase the enterprise's competitiveness and expand the business by offering new or improved products and services.
innovations.target_group: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
● Novice designers affected by the pandemic financially and professionally improve their skills, acquire new knowledge, and establish new contacts.
● Small and medium-size enterprises acquire theoretical knowledge and receive tangible design solutions created according to their needs. Mainly designed solutions increase enterprise competitiveness, enabling them to implement circular and digital economy principles in their business.
● During the project, 34 design solutions meeting sustainability and circular economy principles were created that are simultaneously commercialized, adapted for production, and realized.
● The project's indirect beneficiaries are potential customers of these enterprises who will be able to benefit from sustainable, aesthetic, and convenient design solutions. These products will enable customers to spare funds because their design is adapted for secondary use, using the product without residual, repairing, etc.
● The project demonstrates design's value and might encourage other companies to invest more in design and R&D.

innovations.problem: Barriers to communication by people with physical and mental disabilities.

This will be achieved through the introduction and implementation of assistive technologies for eye control in the CNST for children and youth with disabilities, the creation of a training methodology and program and the necessary resources for them.

Development of specific training activities, with which the necessary skills, competences and knowledge can be acquired. Conducting training sessions with specialized software for people with disabilities. The technological provision of 5 Family Accommodation Centers with eye control systems. Training of 25 children and young people with severe physical disabilities.

innovations.name: The Accessible School Model
innovations.lead: Cooperation Fund Foundation, Institute for Regional Development Foundation (FIRR), Rzeszow Regional Development Agency (RARR - Rzeszowska Agencja Rozwoju Regionalnego), GDAŃSK UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY
innovations.problem:
Approximately 87 million people in the EU have some form of disability, and a significant segment of this population does not enjoy the same life opportunities as others. Schools, workplaces, infrastructure, products, services, and information are not always accessible to them. Such individuals are sometimes treated poorly or unfairly - 52 percent of people with disabilities feel discriminated against.
Most students with disabilities face difficulties in school due to architectural barriers or barriers in the education process. Only 29.4 percent of people with disabilities attain higher education compared to 43.8 percent of those without disabilities. Only half of people with disabilities are employed, while 3 out of 4 people without disabilities are employed. Those who are employed also face barriers in the workplace.
The Accessible School Model is a tool allowing the elimination of barriers in schools and their transformation into a friendly environment for learning and work.
innovations.description:
The Accessible School Model is an innovative tool for the accessibility of educational institutions for individuals with special needs, including those with disabilities. The document was developed by experts in architecture, accessibility, and education in collaboration with the Ministry of Education and other institutions working to promote inclusive education in Poland. It was also tested and implemented by almost two hundred of schools  in Poland.
The model presents a holistic approach to the accessibility of the education process, encompassing architectural infrastructure, equipment accessibility, the accessibility of the education process, and the management of educational institutions. It is based on the idea of universal design in architecture and education but also takes into account the perspective of enhancing the accessibility of existing infrastructure through the use of rational improvements.
It responds to the needs of educational institutions and interest groups that aim to improve the accessibility of education and promote access to inclusive forms of education. It provides ready-made solutions and standards and inspires through good practices.
innovations.target_group: Individuals with disabilities
innovations.beneficiaries: Cooperation Fund Foundation, Institute for Regional Development Foundation (FIRR), Rzeszow Regional Development Agency (RARR - Rzeszowska Agencja Rozwoju Regionalnego), GDAŃSK UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY
innovations.evidence: The Accessible School Model has been implemented in 184 schools and 74 local government units. Thanks to the implementation of the Model, these institutions are ready to conduct the education process for all children and meet their individual needs, including those arising from disabilities. Schools have eliminated existing architectural barriers, raised awareness, and enhanced the qualifications and competencies of staff in the field of inclusive education. As part of the project, publications were developed, including the "Accessible School Model" and a collection of good practices called the "Implementation Handbook." The publications are available in both Polish and English on the website www.dostepnaszkola.info .
authors: Cooperation Fund Foundation, Institute for Regional Development Foundation (FIRR), Rzeszow Regional Development Agency (RARR - Rzeszowska Agencja Rozwoju Regionalnego), GDAŃSK UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY

innovations.name: Remake Textile Project
innovations.problem: The main objective of the project is to create training, employment and entry-level jobs for participants far from the labor market. At the same time, we will effectively address the challenge that will arise as a consequence of the EU Waste Directive on the separate collection of all textile waste by January 1, 2025. We will focus on getting long-term unemployed, refugees and IVAS in Sweden between 21 and 59 years old closer to and entering the labor market in the framework of circular transition, by completing ongoing tests on and for the target group's integration and labor market entry, with the methodological development that will result from the project. The pathways there are collection-sorting-recycling-reuse-upcycling/remake. The further along the circular chain, the higher the potential added value. However, this must be subject to a market with the ability and willingness to pay for the services performed in the circular chain.
innovations.description: The overall objective of the project is to develop innovative solutions for managing the increasing amount of textile waste that municipalities will be responsible for from 2025 onwards. At the same time, it focuses on skills development and recycling training for long-term unemployed people aged between 21 and 59, with good language skills in English or Swedish.
innovations.target_group: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: By integrating circular practices and social inclusion into our project, we aim to find a sustainable circular business model or process for textile recycling that includes a method for labour market integration . Our vision is that the resulting concept will be our final "circular solution" that we aim to identify during the project period.

innovations.name: Zekki digital self-assessment tool for young people wellbeing
innovations.problem:
Approximately one in six young adults ages 20-34, 14 million in total, are not in employment, education or training (NEET) in EU, which means they are unable to find a place in the current education or job market offering. 50 % of 18-29 years olds in the EU had unmet needs for mental health care in 2022.
If support cannot be accessed on time, problems become more complex and prolonged. This can lead to social exclusion (loneliness), marginalisation and resentment towards society. At the same time, the society loses the young person’s potential.
innovations.description:
Zekki collates the available support services and offers them to young people according to their current needs
Zekki offers support for strengthening wellbeing and finding a personal path (independently or with the necessary support).  Zekki can offer clarity to a personal situation, encouragement, appropriate and timely support and help, and a direct pathway to support services. Zekki is offered to young people as an accessible, open and mobile-optimised website, which young people can use to reflect on how they are doing. It is marketed on social media aimed at young people, on the websites of various NGOs (youth services, recreational organisations), and by professionals who work with young people (e.g. teachers, study guidance counsellors, youth workers). Zekki begins with a rapid 3X10D Survey consisting of ten questions. Based on the answers, young person gets encouraging feedback, formulated by professionals, and recommendations for the appropriate services.
innovations.target_group: NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
Young people themselves and the professionals who have used Zekki give very positive feedback. E.g. young people opinions (scale 1-5): Zekki was easy to use: 4.7; Zekki helped me to figure out my situation: 3.5; I got new information or tips of support suitable for me: 3.5; I will use Zekki again: 3.4
In 2021, Zekki won European innovation council's the best European social innovation (EUSIC) award.

innovations.name: Social Innovation Catalyst (Competence Centre for Social Innovation)
innovations.lead: Shipyard Foundation, Foundation for Social and Economic Initiatives (FISE)
innovations.problem:
Innovative ideas are born in every corner of Poland but coming up with an innovative solution is rarely enough. Since 2016 a dozen of social innovation incubators has supported social innovators in Poland, but the cooperation between them and relations with other institutions active on social innovations needed to be strengthened. At that time there was lack of a functioning social innovation ecosystem.
We believed it was crucial to expand the network with different institutions involved in social innovations and create opportunities for cooperation. Only working together, we can build an enabling and innovation-friendly environment, empowering the various actors and incubators and build their capacity to engage in innovation.
Another so far unmet need was quite unsatisfied access of innovators, incubators and other institutions to resources, tools and knowledge on social innovation. Especially for social innovators access to tools and knowledge was often limited by funds and remote locations. Social innovators often feel lonely in their work and misunderstood in their sense of mission. Working in this area also involves a high risk of burnout, frustration and lack of time to take care of own needs.
The need for exchange of knowledge and experience is also felt by those involved in social innovation incubators and other institutions that are active in the area of social innovation in various ways.
innovations.description:
The aim of the Social Innovation Catalyst is to create the most favorable conditions for initiating, developing, disseminating and scaling up social innovations in Poland. We attend to widely inform and promote social innovations as a tool to solve important social problems and try to promote the very concept of 'social innovation', introducing it to the public debate and proposing a common understanding of it.
We support the creation of a social innovation ecosystem based on the principle of networking, not on a hierarchical structure. We do this in a variety of ways. We network people and entities working in this area, including innovators, incubators of social innovations and other institutions.
We support:
people running social innovation incubators; we create a safe space for them to share experiences; we provide knowledge and tools to support the incubation of innovation;
innovators in acquiring or developing the competences needed to implement social innovations. We organize networking meetings, study visits, training and we publish guides for people working in different subject areas.
We organise meetings, conferences, workshops and study visits.
As a part of support for incubators we organized three study visits, to Barcelona, Helsinki and Amsterdam. It was an opportunity for those supporting social innovations to network, get inspired by local solutions and learn about new tools and methods that could be implemented in their work.
In our work we continuously try to identify needs and ambitions of the incubators’ teams and address them in the best way possible through meetings and webinars (face to face and online). Some of the topics we covered were:
how to spread social innovations and how to talk about them in accessible way,
evaluation: experiences with evaluating innovations and practice use of ours and others knowledge and lessons learned,
accessibility: how to take care of it and develop it in the context of social innovation but also how to write easy to read and accessible texts,
sustainability: ideas on how to ensure the sustainability of social innovations,
copyright laws,
anti-burnout workshops.
The first edition of our project, Social Innovation Catalyst , has concluded. However, we are currently running the second edition of the project – Social Innovation Catalyst 2 .
About the new edition:
We believe that many socially important needs require new approaches. Therefore, either independently or by supporting others, we search for, refine, and test innovative solutions in practice – social innovations.
Within the framework of Social Innovation Catalyst 2, we create conditions conducive to the initiation, development, dissemination, and scaling of social innovations in Poland. We support an ecosystem of social innovations based on a network principle rather than a hierarchical structure.
We strive to promote the very concept of “social innovation” in various ways, introducing it into public discourse and proposing a mutually developed understanding of it. We also support individuals and institutions working on their innovative ideas, helping to generate, refine, test, and implement them.
We also carry out our own activities that lead to the creation of innovative methods, solutions, tools, and objects aimed at helping to solve social problems.
We create space and tools to facilitate the exchange of experience, enhance knowledge and skills, and enable the development of networks. We connect individuals and entities active in this field, including innovators and social innovation incubator operators. We organize meetings, conferences, workshops, and study visits.
We are constantly updating a portal (innovacjespoleczne.pl) , which serves as an informative and educational tool for all individuals and institutions working in this sphere. The portal also includes a database of social innovations, enabling the search for projects based on various criteria and promoting the best solutions in the field.

innovations.evidence:
We launched a website www.innowacjespoleczne.pl , which is an important tool to support the information and education of actors active in the field of social innovation.
We created and are still developing a social innovation database containing descriptions and information on innovations worked out and tested within ESF. The database has a dual function: on the one hand, to promote social innovation, and on the other hand, to enable incubators and innovators to search for innovations of interest to them according to specific criteria. As of today, we have already over 1200 entries of tested social innovations in our database, and almost 200 which positively pasted the test and are/were mainstreamed. We are also developing an English version of the website.
We have disseminated and scaled up 7 innovative solutions.
We have supported relations and shared resources , tools and knowledge that will help us co-create a vibrant movement of social innovation in Poland.
We have prepared several guidebooks on i.e. Design Thinking, evaluation, acceleration and communication on social innovation. We also translated into Polish and published couple of foreign publications on innovations and incubation process (such as “Good incubation” or “Development Impact&You. Practical tools to trigger & support social innovation” by NESTA).
Social Innovation Catalyst has its own podcast called “Social Inventions” were we interview innovators, experts and people working daily in the field of social innovation.
As mentioned before beside developing knowledge and competences through workshops and meeting we see the equally big value in connecting people and giving them space to network.
Every year, in the autumn, we organize our flagship event, a two-day meeting called wymIaNNa. The clue of it is in the name which is a wordplay of words “innovation” and “exchange”.
We gather together around 250 innovators, incubators, public officials and other people interested in the topic. The registration is open for everyone, both organizations and private individuals regardless their experience, level of knowledge or geographic location in Poland.
The event is filled with lectures, workshops and sessions conducted largely by the selected participants themselves. There is also time for networking and integration as well as study visits to locally based institutions working with social innovation in search of inspiration and broadening horizons.

sections.question: Evidence
sections.answer:
We launched a website www.innowacjespoleczne.pl , which is an important tool to support the information and education of actors active in the field of social innovation.
We created and are still developing a social innovation database containing descriptions and information on innovations worked out and tested within ESF. The database has a dual function: on the one hand, to promote social innovation, and on the other hand, to enable incubators and innovators to search for innovations of interest to them according to specific criteria. As of today, we have already over 1200 entries of tested social innovations in our database, and almost 200 which positively pasted the test and are/were mainstreamed. We are also developing an English version of the website.
We have disseminated and scaled up 7 innovative solutions.
We have supported relations and shared resources , tools and knowledge that will help us co-create a vibrant movement of social innovation in Poland.
We have prepared several guidebooks on i.e. Design Thinking, evaluation, acceleration and communication on social innovation. We also translated into Polish and published couple of foreign publications on innovations and incubation process (such as “Good incubation” or “Development Impact&You. Practical tools to trigger & support social innovation” by NESTA).
Social Innovation Catalyst has its own podcast called “Social Inventions” were we interview innovators, experts and people working daily in the field of social innovation.
As mentioned before beside developing knowledge and competences through workshops and meeting we see the equally big value in connecting people and giving them space to network.
Every year, in the autumn, we organize our flagship event, a two-day meeting called wymIaNNa. The clue of it is in the name which is a wordplay of words “innovation” and “exchange”.
We gather together around 250 innovators, incubators, public officials and other people interested in the topic. The registration is open for everyone, both organizations and private individuals regardless their experience, level of knowledge or geographic location in Poland.
The event is filled with lectures, workshops and sessions conducted largely by the selected participants themselves. There is also time for networking and integration as well as study visits to locally based institutions working with social innovation in search of inspiration and broadening horizons.

innovations.name: Arbetsintegrering i cirkulärekonomin
innovations.problem: The project aims at the group of people who, due to persistent difficulties in meeting the requirements of today's labor market, need adaptations in their employment. innovations.name: Su la Cler
innovations.problem: It is a big challenge for small companies to find space to operate. On the other hand, there are many properties lying empty which can lead to deprivation. The project seeks to resolve both problems with a single solution. Su la Cler offers a package of free services aimed at: LOCAL MICRO AND SMALL BUSINESSES LOOKING FOR SPACE AT ADVANTAGEOUS CONDITIONS - Acceleration and support to strengthen the company - Staff retraining Support services -Guarantee of good contractual conditions for the rental OWNERS OF COMMERCIAL SPACES LOOKING FOR RELIABLE ENTITIES TO RENT TO - Analysis of context needs -Territorial animation - Opportunity to choose from a portfolio of reliable tenants - Measurement of the social impact generated by the project
innovations.description:
The aim of Su la Cler is to generate a positive and measurable social impact in the neighborhoods of Milan 01Create or grow local micro and small businesses 02 Increase the commercial and service offering where it is absent or insufficient 03 Create good quality jobs, particularly for residents 04 Revitalize neighborhoods while safeguarding their identity The project targets local small enterprises in the areas of retail and services, which will be able to join a free capacity building and support programme with:
Training and support to strengthen their enterprise
Upskilling and reskilling of staff
Supporting services
Favourable lease terms for some ground-floor commercial spaces in the city
innovations.target_group: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: The project expects to generate impact on three fronts: people-enterprises-neighbourhoods, through workforce professional skills development and quality jobs increase, as much as the creation, growth and regeneration of neighbourhood business, and an increase in territorial animation, a leap forward towards the intervention areas' socio-economic regeneration.

innovations.name: Basisbaan Groningen
innovations.problem:
Despite the presence of vacancies there is are still a group experiencing unemployment. We have witnessed that there is a group making various attempts to participate or reintegrate into the workforce, yet they consistently encounter barriers preventing them from securing employment in the traditional labour market.
Nevertheless, we also recognize the abundance of tasks and activities available within our neighborhoods and communities. So we created tasks around our participants that match with the skills they do have.
innovations.description:
The matching procedure is very thorough. We meet with the resident several times to really get to know them and to make the best possible match. We create tasks around our participants that match with the skills they do have. The jobs are tailor made.
We provide intensive support to those in basic jobs. We do this by offering guidance on the job, as well as on various topics such as income, well-being, and the changes one faces when starting work. Tasks that genuinely contribute to the livability of the neighborhood are sourced from within our municipality for the basic job holders to perform.
innovations.target_group: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons
innovations.evidence:
The benefits for these participants are multifaceted: Participants have reported higher levels of self-esteem, improved mental well-being, but they also experience a newfound sense of peace and security.
From a broader perspective, the benefits extend beyond the individual level. For the national government, the initiative translates into lower costs for social security as participants transition from welfare to gainful employment. Additionally, increased income from taxes further strengthens government revenues.
Our program is not designed as a temporary fix or a springboard to other opportunities. We’ve learned from the participant that this approach provides them with a sense of stability, it relieves stress. We provide ongoing support and mentorship to help participants succeed in their roles.
Furthermore, we recognize that one size does not fit all when it comes to employment. That's why the jobs offered through the Basisbaan Initiative are tailor-made to fit the skills and interests of each participant. If a job is not suitable for a participant, we work closely with them to identify alternative opportunities or make adjustments to their current role.
This is one of the main reasons why we have not experienced any exits other than reaching retirement age or participant who died.
In summary, the Basisbaan has proven to be a valuable investment in both human capital and social welfare, by providing meaningful employment opportunities. While there are associated costs, the returns in terms of individual well-being, community development, and economic sustainability justify the continued support and expansion of such initiatives.

innovations.name: Uppsala Yrkesmentor
innovations.problem: The addressed problem revolves around the persistent issue of unemployment among foreign-born women, which has significant individual and societal consequences. Foreign-born women encounter specific barriers hindering their entry into the labor market, as well as opportunities to secure fair wages and safe working conditions. This issue is exacerbated by challenges in social and economic integration, which take longer for foreign-born women compared to men. Despite efforts by various agencies, there remains a gap between the demands of the labor market and the educational and professional backgrounds of foreign-born women. Structural, organizational, and individual factors, including gender, age, migration status, education, and previous work experience, compound the difficulty of successful integration processes. Addressing this multifaceted problem requires a comprehensive approach, focusing on soft skills, education, networking, and combating discrimination to facilitate foreign-born women's entry into the workforce.
innovations.description: We propose a solution that involves integrating multiple interventions to enhance outcomes for foreign-born women. The project combines mentorship during vocational training with ongoing collaboration with the target audience. The project will also arrange women's gatherings where all participants and mentors are invited, as a way to create networking opportunities. Foreign-born women enrolled in three selected vocational training programs in Uppsala municipality will be provided with a mentor during 6 months of their education. The mentor's role is to support participants during their training, aiming to increase completion rates and provide valuable insights into the profession, as well as networking opportunities. The chosen vocational fields—childcare, culinary arts, and healthcare—are areas with high demand and are considered shortage occupations in Sweden. Through continuous refinement based on knowledge acquisition and active involvement of the target group, this method aims to address the multifaceted challenges faced by foreign-born women in integrating into the workforce effectively.
innovations.target_group: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals experiencing gender marginalization
innovations.evidence: The goal is that the women participating in the project will include an increased number of foreign-born women completing their vocational training and subsequently entering the workforce. By integrating mentorship with vocational education, the initiative aims to foster social and professional networks, enhance knowledge, provide supportive environments, facilitate language training, boost motivation and self-esteem, and tailor support to the needs and preferences of the target group.

innovations.name: Fostering Digital Marketing Cooperatives
innovations.problem: Big Dreams is included in this initiative, and the programs were initiated in 2022 as a pilot experience to promote youth entrepreneurship, given the difficulties young people face in starting their own businesses, including lack of experience, lack of family/social support, and lack of funding.
innovations.description:
The support of Social Economy institutions led by CEPES is also noteworthy. It is considered a good practice because it includes:
Impact through sustainable integration into the labor market for unemployed young people, especially those at risk of social exclusion and those from marginalized communities, enrolled in the National Youth Guarantee System.
Promotion of employability and professional skills of young people not employed and not integrated into education or training systems.
Impact on job creation with the incorporation of digital marketing professionals into companies and support for the Spanish economy.
Promotion of self-employment and collective entrepreneurship through work cooperatives.
High degree of coverage, reaching all of Spain in a face-to-face format.
Collaboration between different entities in the productive ecosystem: large companies, regional business associations, sector companies.
innovations.target_group: NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training)
innovations.evidence:
2022: 95 youth trained . 49 women y 49 men
2023: 81 youth trained .38 women y 28 men

innovations.name: The Break Fellowship
innovations.problem:
Gender gap within the EU entrepreneurial ecosystem.
Territorial gap. Fostering talent capitalsation in medium and small towns as well as in rural areas
innovations.description:
The Break is not a standard internationalization/softlanding program. It aims to create systemic changes. The values of the Breakers are the foundation of everything: B (Brave), R (Regenerative), E (Empathetic), A (Aligned), K (Kind), E (Enthusiastic), R (Rebellious), S (Self-Compassionate ). Based on these values, a community of collaboration, sisterhood, and mutual support is formed. The relationships they build among themselves are likely to last for years, and most of them feel empowered to continue advancing in closing the gender gap.
These values and tools for systemic change and regenerative economy are transmitted to the HCs in a previous Training of Trainers, using the U Theory as a basis.
The talent of the Breakers is capitalized to solve specific challenges in the communities that host them through open innovation sessions. Stakeholders from the community are involved in these sessions (depending on the challenge: municipalities, regional governments, NGOs, local associations, and residents themselves). This promotes the integration of the Breakers through Service Learning. The proposed solutions have mostly been absorbed by local institutions to ensure their sustainability.
The Break aims to be CO2-neutral in 2023 and is replicable in any country.
innovations.target_group: Individuals experiencing gender marginalization
innovations.evidence:
• Internationalization: 40% of the Breakers have generated leads with local actors in Spain, and 35% have formed alliances. 52.3% have created business alliances with other participants from The Break in the EU.
• Local impact: HCs have strengthened their strategy with a rating of 4 out of 5, opening the door to new projects. Most HCs have expanded their workforce thanks to the program.
• Breakers' acceleration: 68% rate their project's maturity as 4 out of 5, thanks to The Break. Those who only had an MVP were able to formally establish their company. 92.3% of the 2022 projects are still alive six months later.
• Job creation in the EU: The average number of people in The Break's entrepreneurial projects is 2. According to a survey conducted after six months (since November 2022), it is inferred that the personnel growth in the Breakers' companies was at least 50%.
• Community of 1,000 entrepreneurs: After the program's completion in 2023, the virtual community will continue to be energized for mutual support and the promotion of systemic changes.
• Community of 30 Spanish HCs: HCs have created a network to develop projects beyond The Break.
To learn about the project's impact, please visit LinkedIn ( #TheBreakFellowship ), Instagram ( TheBreakFellowship).

innovations.name: A Blind Spot
innovations.lead: Administration for Social Welfare in the north-east of Gothenburg
innovations.problem: Girl and young women who are in or near the gang criminal environment is overseen. The girls that can be for example girlfriends, wives, sisters, cousins, friends, and mothers of men in gangs are generally seen as victims. As well as girls who did not grow up in the vulnerable neighborhoods but for other reasons are in a vulnerable situation and are drawn into the environment through, for example, nightclubs, hotel parties organized by gang criminals, in connection with drug dealing or other risk environments. The girls' situation is not noticed to a high enough and the vulnerability they may find themselves in is often overlooked, as is the role the girls play in organized crime. To prevent long-term social and economic exclusion of the target group the situation of girls who live or are in the gang criminal context needs to be noticed. This requires the development of new approaches, new tools, and new skills that captures and adapts to the target group's situation and needs.
innovations.description:
The overall objective of the project is to contribute to the inclusion and well-being of young girls at risk of long-term socio-economic vulnerability. Support their increased empowerment and participation in society and their ability to influence their own future. This requires a new approach and collaboration between social actors such as example social services, police and health care to develop knowledge, new tools, and new skills that capture and are adapted to the girl’s situation and needs. The project, as a social innovation, aims to develop the ability of social actors to identify and make available cross-cutting gender-sensitive social support aimed at young girls in a gang environment. Through social innovative approaches, the project will develop new forms of community support aimed at the target group.
Project objectives:
1. Develop and test a new gender-sensitive way of working to discover and support girls an young women in the gang-related context that is at risk of crime, vulnerability, victimization and support them for education and work.
2. Develop cooperation and consensus between social actors through developed knowledge and competence about the target group's situation and needs.
3. Disseminate the project's method at local, regional, national, and European level.
innovations.target_group: Individuals experiencing gender marginalization
innovations.beneficiaries: Administration for Social Welfare in the north-east of Gothenburg
innovations.evidence: The goal is for the girls, who are associated or affiliated with organized crime and who are at risk of long-term socio-economic vulnerability, to engage in their own education and establish themselves in the labor market.
authors: Administration for Social Welfare in the north-east of Gothenburg

innovations.name: Demografieberatung Digi+
innovations.problem:
Our work environment has changed significantly in recent years. Digitization, labor shortages, an aging society, and waves of retirement pose great challenges for businesses. The Demografieberatung Digi+ supports companies and their employees in facing these changes. As part of the consultation, we work together with company representatives to develop a stable corporate strategy and use change and digitization to ensure the competitiveness of businesses and to adapt jobs and workforce to digital and demographic changes.
Demografieberatung Dig+:
creates an awareness of the impact of digitalization and demographics in businesses,
promotes age-appropriate and life-phase-oriented work environments so that jobs, companies, entrepreneurs, and workers can effectively respond to demographic and digital changes,
and uses digitalization and digital support tools as an opportunity to create age-independent jobs, new possibilities for work organization, and promote the digital skills of employees through consultation (referring to tailored digital further education opportunities).
innovations.description:
The consulting services are free of charge and can be used by all companies based in Austria (except Burgenland). Depending on the needs, different target groups are the focus of the consultation, such as employees, managers, HR managers, or works council members.
We look at the challenges at the operational level, at the level of management, and at the level of employees and focus on digital and age-appropriate design in the areas of work organization, leadership and corporate culture, personnel management, knowledge and skills, and health.
The implementation of the measures is individually tailored to the company's challenges, goals, and resources in every consultation. In order to sensitize and empower the company to work on the issues independently and respond to change even after the consultation is completed, the affected employee groups are involved in all phases of the consultation. This is done through surveys, workshops, coaching, and tandem work to address the issues.
One key innovation of the implementation is our " Angebots- und Förderlandkarte " (Offer and Support Map). The interactive map collects offers and support that businesses and employees in Austria can take advantage of. This includes regional, national, and international support in the areas of skills development and training, digitalization and innovation support, support for women and people with disabilities, support for start-ups, or support for projects to increase ecological sustainability. We use a web crawler to collect the content.
innovations.target_group: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
The key results are:
930 advised companies
5-10% of the advised companies are start-ups
Main target group are employees over 45 years old
At least 50% of all employees involved in the implementation are womenn
Through demographic consulting Dig+, companies receive:
100% funded customized consulting services,
complete analysis of the age structure of the workforce,
analysis of hotspots and challenges in the company,
empowerment and enablement for self-help,
mediation of further offers and support from our partners.
Companies and employees have access to:
Regional events for networking and exchange for companies
Conferences with workshops and international experts
Toolbox with over 60 tools
Videos, webinars, and learning paths

innovations.name: 100 Percent – Equality pays off.
innovations.lead: Deloitte Consulting, BAB Unternehmensberatung GmbH, ÖSB Consulting GmbH
innovations.problem:
The plain fact is that there are still significant differences in income between men and women in Austria. Our gender pay gap is still well above the EU average. And although the proportion of women actively in work is converging on that of men, this is not reflected in the career development of women.
The primary aim of the project is to attain equality between women and men in order that everyone can fulfil their true potential. This brings advantages for all - the companies, their employees and the Austrian labor market.
The professional design of transparent remuneration systems and fair career opportunities make an important contribution to this. To achieve this “100 Percent – Equality pays off” offers consultations for companies to design transparent remuneration systems and fair career opportunities. This advisory service is free of charge for participating companies.
innovations.description:
Each company participating in the program has a ‘100 Percent’ contact person who guides them through the entire advisory process. Depending upon the focus of the specific consultation with a company, other advisors with specialist expertise in the areas of equality, income, career and career planning are called upon as necessary.
‘100 Percent’ guides companies through four phases:
1. Professional data analysis and determining the present situation:
At the beginning of the consultation, a comprehensive data analysis provides companies with a picture of the status quo with regard to the equality between women and men in terms of career and income within the company.
The analysis consists of the following sub-areas:
Workforce structure analysis by gender (BESTRA)
Salary structure analysis by gender (GESTRA)
Maturity level with regard to career from an equality perspective
Maturity level with regard to income from an equality perspective
Organizational / structural anchoring of equality
Typology & motivation with regard to equality
​The results of this status quo analysis are summarized in a Results Report, which is presented to the company in a joint reflection meeting with the case manager.
2. Defining targets and selecting the advisory topics
Building on the findings from the data analysis, the company and case manager jointly determine the focus of the further consultation and thus tailor the advisory services to the company’s needs. The consulting content is divided into three consulting packages and can be flexibly combined:
Advisory package Basics of Equality: This package is a compulsory part of the consultation process and gives companies basic insights into the legal framework with regard to equality as well as into the economic and corporate benefits of gender equality.
Advisory package Career: Companies can choose from six consulting modules and thus work specifically on their individual career processes. The modules are in-depth career analysis, recruiting, leadership, career development, time out management and internal & external communication.
Advisory package Income: Companies can choose from the following six consulting modules to work specifically on equality-oriented design of the remuneration system and salary processes: in-depth income analysis, job evaluation, leadership, salary development, performance evaluation, internal & external communication.
3. Optional career advice for female employees
As part of the optional career consultation, companies have the opportunity to specifically promote individual female employees. Depending on the number of employees to be advised, they receive special coaching on the subject of career planning in individual and / or group settings from career advisors.
The consulting content is divided into four consulting modules:
Leadership
Career development
Time out management
Future of Work
The aim of this optional career advice is, in addition to working on corporate structures and processes, to promote female employees in their career development on an individual level and thus to develop 100 percent of their potential.
4. Ensuring sustainability and conclusion of the consultation
The consultation process concludes with the handover of the final report and a joint reflection meeting. As a measure to ensure quality and sustainability, companies can work out an equality strategy together with their consultant. This ensures that measures promoting equality develop their full effect.
All Austrian companies can benefit from Peer2Peer events , regardless of whether they participated in the consultation. Over the course of the project, these events are organized in the project regions on various topics for companies and employees. In addition to specialist input from experts on current HR and remuneration topics, the Peer2Peer events offer the opportunity to network with other companies, exchange views on issues relating to equality in the workplace and continuously learn from each
innovations.target_group: Individuals experiencing gender marginalization
innovations.beneficiaries: Deloitte Consulting, BAB Unternehmensberatung GmbH, ÖSB Consulting GmbH
innovations.evidence:
With the professional design of transparent remuneration systems and fair career opportunities, 126 companies have succeeded in exploring their full potential - both within the existing workforce and on the labor market. 75% of the participating companies were SMEs (< 250 employees), 25% were large companies (> 250 employees).
In addition, 58 companies provided their female employees with career advice to support them in their career development on an individual level.
Over the course of the project, 59 regional press articles , over 270 posts on social media and 6 videos were published.
Around 80 companies were able to network at the Peer2Peer events.

innovations.name: FairPlusService
innovations.lead: ÖSB Consulting GmbH, ABZ*AUSTRIA, the update training GmbH, ÖSB Social Innovation gemeinnützige GmbH
innovations.problem:
The Covid-19 pandemic has had a severe impact on the social sector, particularly on (private) nurseries. In the federal state of Lower Austria, FairPlusService advised several companies in this sector that were able to benefit from the project on various levels.
On the one hand, the needs of the companies were addressed at an individual level. Employer expertise was strengthened in order to counteract the acute labour shortage. Coaching sessions were organised to address the increasing psychological and physical stress experienced by employees.
Secondly, the participating companies were deliberately networked with each other for the first time in this form in our peer-to-peer events, which were specially developed for the sector. The event focussed on the exchange and discussion of the particular challenges for childcare facilities as well as good practices for retaining female employees (e.g. improved work-life balance, further training opportunities), equality-oriented recruitment (e.g. attracting men to the female-dominated profession). Support for more intensive company networking and the development of a joint approach for applications to interest groups and the state of Lower Austria was also essential.
In the Industrieviertel Süd region, there was also a high density of companies that employ women with a migration background. The challenges in this area are manifold (lack of language skills, different rituals and holidays, different values, ...). This was also taken into account on an individual company level through workshops developed for this purpose (e.g. Diversity Picnic) as well as at group level. Here, too, networking events were held with companies from different sectors but with similar problems in order to exchange ideas and implement good practices.
innovations.description:
The FairPlus approach, which has been tried and tested throughout Austria, combines counselling modules for company managers with coaching units and compact training courses for female employees, which enable further training and (higher) qualifications for previously disadvantaged groups of women. Networking and public relations work also promote equality between women and men. Special focus was put on winning over small and medium-sized enterprises to our project. The target group of women with lower formal qualifications has rarely been the focus of publicly funded programmes.
Our project goals include equal opportunities for all, particularly in terms of access to education and training, fair working conditions and integration and inclusion. Our counselling approach focuses on supporting empowerment top down and empowerment bottom up. The companies are supported in their employer competence and recognise equality as an asset for their further development. For example, as part of our consulting services, companies addressed previously unrecognised horizontal and vertical segregation, differences in participation in further training, etc. for the first time. The analyses were followed by the planning and implementation of targeted improvements. Women with low formal qualifications were also often offered group and individual coaching sessions for the first time in order to provide them with the best possible support on their path to further training and a career.
innovations.target_group: Individuals experiencing gender marginalization
innovations.beneficiaries: ÖSB Consulting GmbH, ABZ*AUSTRIA, the update training GmbH, ÖSB Social Innovation gemeinnützige GmbH
innovations.evidence:
Low wage means earning less than two thirds of the average income (around €1,740, close to the at-risk-of-poverty rate). In Austria, significantly more women than men are employed in the low-wage sector: 25% vs. 8%. The gender difference is the greatest in the EU.
In labour-intensive low-wage sectors such as retail, cleaning, catering and care, more than 50% of the employees are women, often with lower formal qualifications, with a history of migration and/or de-skilled. However, these sectors also offer low-threshold access to the labour market and integration opportunities.
This is where FairPlusService comes in and supports companies in recognising further training and careers as a development opportunity, even for employees with low formal qualifications. In view of high inflation and increasing digitalisation, the importance of lifelong learning remains high.

innovations.name: NEETsLAB (ended)
innovations.lead: South-Eastern Finland University of Applied Sciences
innovations.problem: The application of the innovative practice aims to find solutions to problems in the areas of the labor market and social inclusion of NEETs by transferring a social innovation and developing a new solution (model). Suggestions and advice are given on how to avoid risks and barriers when working with young people under 29 who fall into the NEET group.
innovations.target_group: NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training)
innovations.beneficiaries: South-Eastern Finland University of Applied Sciences
innovations.evidence: New tools create a supportive environment for young people to participate fully in public life, achieving their full potential. The foundations are laid for the long-term overcoming of the challenges facing young people who are not working and not engaged in learning and training. One of the main problems of the representatives of the NEETs society, caused by the lack of support from the circle of people surrounding them and distrust in themselves, has been overcome. Subsequently, they are not afraid to show themselves to the public and reveal what skills they possess. Observations prove the statement that when inactive youth are supported, they reveal their potential in various spheres – digital world, art activities, photography, cooking, clubhouses. The lack of qualifications among this community very often leads to the large number of unemployed or inactive persons among them, depressing them to never get out of this status. However, their support was able to contribute to reaching the inner world of each of the young people. Based on the considered innovation, it can be concluded that innovation is the most powerful tool for improving any kind of processes, including and quality processes – innovation is such an innovation that improves quality and reduces costs (and price), i.e. increases competitiveness. NGO "Peonies", as a beneficiary of the current project, is aware that to increase the scale of the impact of social innovation, a different way of thinking is required, as well as a different way of financing. The main conclusions that can be drawn from testing the innovation are: - Innovation is something new that has not been done before in the country; - Digital mentoring is a current topic and tool that is increasingly attracting the attention of institutions such as the Directorate of the Regional Employment Service, the Directorate of the Labor Bureau, Social Services; - Clubhouses reveal hidden potentials of young people, including those with disabilities, to contribute to their realization on the labor market in the future; - Interest groups contribute to attracting the target groups to specific activities, obtaining new theoretical and practical knowledge and their professional development in this field; - Reward indicator for the number of persons involved in testing the innovation; - Unceasing desire on the part of the youth to continue the activities between them and their mentors even after the end of the project.

innovations.raw_text:
NEETsLAB (ended)
The application of the innovative practice aims to find solutions to problems in the areas of the labor market and social inclusion of NEETs by transferring a social innovation and developing a new solution (model). Suggestions and advice are given on how to avoid risks and barriers when working with young people under 29 who fall into the NEET group.
The goals of the project meet the needs of the target groups (inactive youth from 15 to 29 years of age) to increase their social status, their knowledge and skills for active inclusion in the labor market and those of the partners to build partnership and cooperation skills for solving general employment problems of the most vulnerable groups on the labor market, namely young people from 15 to 29 years of age. Working panels have been developed: Panel 1 "The paths in our life" - includes 10 meetings lasting 4 hours and aims to help the mentors to help the young people themselves to define the path of their life. Panel 2 "Learning through play" - has a duration of 10 meetings of 4 hours each, and the aim is to apply developed game techniques to increase the self-awareness and feelings of young people from the group of NEETs for active inclusion and active participation. Panel 3 "Assessment, Inspiration and Dissemination" - The aim is to gather experience-based information about the causes negatively affecting the lives of young boys and to create methods, together with their help, to increase their independence in the real work environment they will find themselves in. Within the framework of the developed social innovation "New models for mentoring through the transfer of intelligence between generations", 3 tools for individual and group mentoring of NEETs were created, which were successfully tested on 20 inactive youth up to 29 years old. The tools are as follows: - Individual digital mentoring via the Facebook and Discord platforms - Interest groups: Photography, Cooking and Art activities - Clubhouses A total of 32 individuals participated in the testing, some of whom expressed a willingness to participate in more than 1 of the new instruments.
This study case intends to scale up or transfer its activities to similar organisations in other countries, by applying the developed manuals and established good practices. They are as follows:
Мethodology for transfer of social innovation MATTI;
Guide to working with the target group;
New innovation INNO_MENTOR, including 3 tools for individual and group mentoring of NEETs:
- Individual digital mentoring via the Facebook and Discord platforms - Interest groups: Photography, Cooking and Art activities - Clubhouses

innovations.name: Gathering Forces for Increased Youth Employment
innovations.problem: Securing a job is not a given for many young people. A lack of understanding, a lack of role models, inefficient processes, prejudice and segregation are just some of the many challenges that a young person can face in trying to find a job. These trends are reflected in the increasing youth unemployment rates in Sweden, with young people from socio-economically disadvantaged areas notably being the worst affected. At the same time, social entrepreneurs are sitting on innovative solutions to address these issues, but are struggling to find sustainable long-term models to support their successful scaling.
innovations.description: This project sees effective cross-sectoral collaboration as the solution to the above challenges- collaboration which promotes a more equal and non-discriminatory labour market for young people. Social entrepreneurs and municipalities have potential to jointly address social challenges in an effective way, but find difficulties to understand and exploit each others’ strengths and weaknesses. This project builds upon a previous initiative, implemented by Reach for Change and Right by Me and financed by Delegation against segregation, which aimed to gain insights into existing barriers and brainstorm new potential models of collaboration between the two different types of stakeholders. Together with Eskilstuna municipality, we now test and refine a model of collaboration for implementation and dissemination among other municipalities in Sweden.
innovations.target_group: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training)
innovations.evidence: Workshops and capacity development activities will bring together youth leaders and youth participants to foster stronger attitudes and self-confidence related to taking on working life. Through the conceptualisation, testing and dissemination of the collaboration model itself, we hope to prove that it is possible to tackle increasing youth unemployment through such effective collaboration. Through these ambitious objectives we hope to also inspire others to adopt innovative approaches to effective collaboration, seeing a large potential for dissemination to other contexts and geographic locations.

innovations.name: KYKY 2015-2019
innovations.problem:
The KYKY projects, conducted by the City of Helsinki Education Division from 2015 to 2019, aimed to promote the social inclusion of unemployed parents from Somali, Arabic and Kurdish Communities . The objective was to prevent their social exclusion by developing services that facilitate the education and employment of this specific target group. These projects were being executed at Helsinki Vocational College and Adult Institute .
The primary focus of the initiative was on parents who are responsible for caring for their children at home, with Somali, Arabic or Kurdish as their native language. Additionally, the project targeted unemployed immigrant parents who speak Somali, Arabic, or Kurdish and have completed their integration period.
Helsinki has long been concerned about the inadequate integration and social exclusion risks faced by this target group. Immigrant women, especially those with a refugee background, exhibit a low employment rate. In 2014, only 46 percent of individuals who had migrated to Finland from Africa and the Middle East were employed, in stark contrast to the 74 percent employment rate among those with Finnish roots. Women with a refugee background encounter particular obstacles when attempting to re-enter the job market. innovations.name: Take the First Step
innovations.problem:
Despite having the highest rate of third level attainment in the European Union, Ireland still has unmet literacy, numeracy and digital literacy needs among its adult population.  The most recent PIAAC 2012 Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies Survey Results for Ireland showed that 18% of adults (aged 16 to 65) struggle with reading and understanding everyday text. 25% struggle with using maths in everyday life. 42% of adults struggle with basic digital tasks. There are also language needs amongst many adults where English is a Second or Other Language (ESOL).
Recent data from Ireland‘s Central Statistics Office shows that currently there are 320,050 people (aged 25 to 64 years) who have less than a Quality and Qualifications Ireland (QQI) Level 4 qualification (equivalent to a Leaving Certificate). These include 175,640 in employment and 7,990 (2.5%) unemployed; and 131,460 (41%) not engaged in the labour force.
innovations.description: ‘Take the First Step’ was innovative because it created a multi-channel communications campaign to reach the hardest to reach adults through significant spend to create assets and target advertising.  Its messaging drew from the lived experiences of adults who had returned to education to improve their reading, writing, maths or technology skills. It used a range of channels, particularly local radio, to reduce the stigma associated with unmet literacy needs and encourage adults to call a freephone number or go to their local Education and Training Board (ETB) to get advice and information about educational opportunities that responded to their needs.  The campaign was evaluated each year and was adapted based on the findings and the changing circumstances during the COVID-19 pandemic.
innovations.target_group: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
The reach and impact of the ‘Take the First Step’ campaign was high over the five years.  In the final year of the campaign, 4.7 million people were reached through public relations and media activity.  There were 5,085,050 impressions and 836,674 video views of social media and Google ads. Amongst those surveyed with unmet needs, 68% recalled the campaign.
The campaign was regarded as highly effective at encouraging people to seek help and raise awareness of  local free classes.  For instance, during the September to end November 2020 period, NALA received 550 calls to its Freephone number, close to 150% increase on the 2019 number. There were 21,000 users on the dedicted campaign website, takethefirststep.ie.

innovations.name: AdoptIDee
innovations.problem: As we get older our creativity tends to reduce. Our experiences in life, own motivation and structures we are used to live often have a negative influence on our creativity. Also local entrepreneurs struggle with issues but aren't equipped with the right amount of creativity that could really give an out-of-the-box solution for their problems.That's why we need young people because they are not hampered by these effects and trully have pure ideas.
innovations.description: By offering a six-step approach we connect the local entrepreneur with a class of a local school. Each class adopts one entrepreneur and in groups of 4 to 5 students they work on a solution for the problem of the local entrepreneur. Because the average class consists of approx. 20 children, each entrepreneur receives up to 4 or 5 original solutions. One of the steps within the six-step approach is that the children as well as the teacher will visit the local entrepreneur to introduce the children to the workings of a company in an early age. Also it stimulates the regional coherence.

innovations.name: European Network of Innovation for Inclusion
innovations.lead: Acción contra el Hambre (Action Against Hunger Spain)
innovations.problem:
Across the EU, many organisations are working to develop more effective approaches to tackling unemployment and the exclusion and invisibilisation of vulnerable groups in the labour market. For years, these organisations have called for a platform to exchange experiences, identify partners and access information on European funding opportunities and programme calls.
In this context, over its 10 years of existence, the Network has contributed to building a more innovative social inclusion ecosystem by supporting organisations in the development of successful employability and social inclusion programmes and projects. Moreover, the Network offers open access and participation around social innovation, enabling smaller organisations or those with less experience in European projects to incorporate and work on innovative approaches into their interventions. Finally, this networking model enhances the visibility of the Network’s priorities at European level and improves the quality of the partnerships that emerge within it.
innovations.target_group: Other target groups
innovations.beneficiaries: Acción contra el Hambre (Action Against Hunger Spain)
innovations.evidence:
The European Network for Innovation for Inclusion offers its members:
Access to updated information on European funding opportunities related to the social and labour inclusion of vulnerable groups, as well as support in identifying partner organisations for joint project proposals and strategic alliances.
Greater visibility for initiatives and activities of interest to other members through the Network’s online resource bank and communication channels, including social media.
Participation in a capacity building space offering tailored learning opportunities to strengthen skills in social innovation and scaling, including training modules, specialised resources, live sessions and peer exchange.
Opportunities to join Social Innovation Labs, where organisations collaborate to transfer, replicate and scale successful social innovations across different European contexts.
Participation in the Network’s annual event, the Forum on Experiences and Trends in Innovation for Inclusion , open to the wider public and designed as a key networking space. In November 2025, its XIII edition gathered more than 70 in-person participants and reached over 350 total views.

innovations.name: Vives Emplea Saludable
innovations.lead: Acción contra el Hambre (Action Against Hunger Spain)
innovations.problem:
In 2018, Acción Contra el Hambre and the EPINUT research group of the Universidad Complutense de Madrid observed that unemployed people had worse health conditions, compared to the employed population, and that, at the same time, this fact could influence their employability. In other words, unemployment and job insecurity do not only affect the economic well-being of people in a situation of social vulnerability, but also lead to a worsening of their physical, emotional, and social health. Against this background, socio-occupational insertion programmes were identified as a suitable resource for the incorporation of other activities that could have an impact on the health of the most vulnerable groups.
Between 2018 and 2019, a small pilot intervention was carried out in the San Cristóbal de los Ángeles neighbourhood (Villaverde, Madrid). During the intervention, improvements were recorded in terms of exercise, diet quality and the physical, mental, and social wellbeing, reducing the degree of emotional problems that interfered with daily performance.
Finally, in 2020, with the support of the European Social Fund (ESF), Acción contra el Hambre launched a Social Innovation project: Vives Emplea Saludable, whose objective was to redefine the entire model of the socio-occupational insertion itinerary to integrate health education in all its components in a cross-cutting manner, paying special attention to nutrition, physical activity, and self-care. In addition to working intensively on basic competences and people's abilities in the search for employment, Vives Emplea Saludable proposes actions and activities to promote a healthy lifestyle that provides resources and knowledge, allowing the acquisition and improvement of healthy habits, to multiply the possibilities of access to the labour market for the participants. All this also helps people or social groups not only to obtain employment, but also to maintain it in the longer term, thus being able to escape from the situation of risk of social exclusion.
innovations.description:
As defined by the WHO, health is not only the absence of disease, but encompasses physical, mental, and social well-being. It is not unusual for employability projects to promote the emotional and/or social well-being of their participants, as socio-economic differences have a clear impact on health. However, employment pathways have tended to ignore physical wellbeing. This is where innovation is born with Vives Emplea Saludable.
This project develops a multi-component health intervention including emotional well-being, physical activity, balanced nutrition, sleep, and quality rest. Each of these factors influences all areas of our lives, including employment or the search for employment. Thus, this programme offers comprehensive support to its participants with the aim of acting on the causes and effects of hunger by guaranteeing their livelihoods through quality employment. With a dynamic, participatory, and experiential methodology, this project contributes to the goal of social inclusion based on the transformative pillar of health.
The project was formulated following an innovative approach from its conceptualization stage, seeking to design new solutions to the problem of unemployment and its health consequences and the other way around. Based on the analysis of the opportunities that our traditional employment pathways offered and of the social challenges faced, the idea of incorporating the focus on healthy living was generated. This new model was initially tested in a pilot intervention in 2018, delivering excellent results for the participants and demonstrating to be a valuable innovative solution. After that successful pilot intervention, and to date, Vives Emplea Saludable has been scaled up in Spain and incorporated into numerous employment pathways projects of Acción contra el Hambre.
innovations.target_group: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.beneficiaries: Acción contra el Hambre (Action Against Hunger Spain)
innovations.evidence:
The beneficial effects that Vives Emplea Saludable has on users have been confirmed through a scientific study conducted by Acción contra el Hambre and the EPINUT research group of the Universidad Complutense de Madrid. Some of the key results and benefits are the following:
Integrating health education in a transversal way in the social and labour insertion programmes improves healthy habits, self-awareness, and satisfaction of people at risk of exclusion, while maintaining their level of employability. As an illustration, there was a 42.3% of job placements in the intervention group (Vives Emplea Saludable) and 40.0% in the control group (Vives Emplea).
At the beginning of the research, nearly half of the more than 1,000 unemployed people who participated in the sample were overweight and 53% had some level of food insecurity, a percentage that was slightly reduced at the end of the process.
In the group that received physical and mental health care activities, the number of people with good eating habits increased by 26%, an improvement that was not seen among those who did not receive such training.
Those who received health education increased their intake of fruit, vegetables, legumes, nuts, wholegrain cereals and fish, decreased their intake of soft drinks, red meat or sugary breakfasts, skipped fewer meals and paid more attention to reading food labelling.
The employment pathway focused on health and self-care managed to reduce the number of sedentary people, stimulate almost all their physical activity markers, and increase the quality of their rest.
Participants in the healthy programme recorded a 10-18% improvement in all indicators of emotional and social well-being over the course of the project, while those in other employment pathways remained stable or even worsened.
The percentage of people declaring themselves satisfied with life increased by 16% in the intervention group, while in the control group it remained unchanged.
